memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When you have eaten and are satisfied, praise the Lord your God for the good land he has given you. - Deut 8:10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a simple but profound instruction: "When you have eaten and are satisfied, praise the Lord." When you are full, when your needs are met, when life is comfortable — that is the moment to turn your heart in praise to God. It is a call to let satisfaction lead to gratitude, to remember the Giver precisely when we are enjoying the gifts.

This is wiser than it first appears, because fullness is a spiritually dangerous moment. In hunger and need, we naturally cry out to God. But in satisfaction, we can easily forget Him, growing content with the gifts while overlooking the Giver. Moses knew this, so he taught Israel to build gratitude into their moments of plenty. Praise was to rise not only from the depths of need but from the heights of blessing.

There is a beautiful practice hidden in this verse — the habit of giving thanks when we are satisfied. This is why so many believers pause to thank God before or after a meal. It is a small act, but it trains the heart to remember God in the ordinary moments of plenty. Jesus Himself gave thanks before He broke bread (Matt 15:36). When you finish a good meal, when a need is met, when you feel content — let that fullness become a doorway to praise. Gratitude in the moment of satisfaction keeps our hearts tethered to the God who provides.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I remember to praise God when I am satisfied, not only when I am in need?
- How can I build gratitude into the ordinary moments of plenty?
- What simple habit of thanksgiving could I begin this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me to praise You not only in my need but in my fullness. When I am satisfied and content, turn my heart to gratitude, remembering that every good thing comes from You. Keep me tethered to You in the moments of plenty. Amen.
